name: column-wheel-heart-reset
title: Column Wheel Heart Reset
description: A self-cycling confirm/save chip built as a chronograph's column wheel plus heart-cam reset — a needle runs, then a hammer snaps it back to exactly zero on contact regardless of where it stopped, holds, and runs again.
instruction: Build <ColumnWheelHeartReset label? size? trigger? paused? className?> as a small self-cycling SVG feedback chip modeled on a chronograph's column wheel and heart-cam reset. A column wheel is a small toothed wheel with radial pillars; each pusher press indexes it one notch (6 columns here, 60deg/index) via a jumper spring dropping into the valley between pillars. Reset engages a heart-shaped cam fixed to the seconds pinion: a hammer snaps against the heart's point and forces the pinion to rotate to EXACTLY zero regardless of where it stopped — a genuinely self-correcting mechanical return, not an eased tween to a known value. ONE PURE CLOCK, computeFrame(msIntoCycle), drives every moving part; the rAF loop only ever writes the resulting angles straight to SVG <g> ref.style.transform (no React state on the hot path — matches the project's established hot-path rule). Idle cycle: CYCLE_MS=4500, STEP_MS=750 (6 column-wheel steps). Steps 0-3 are RUN: the wheel index advances every 750ms (wheelAngle eases via smoothstep over WHEEL_SNAP_MS=200ms then holds) while a thin needle geared to the same shaft as the heart cam beneath it sweeps CONTINUOUSLY at RUN_STEP_DEG=128deg/step — 128 is deliberately not a divisor of 360, so after 4 run steps needle+cam sit at 512deg mod 360 = 152deg, nowhere near zero, making the reset's snap-to-0 a real visible correction rather than a coincidence. The hammer's rest pose during RUN sits at its ordinary disengaged clearance (HAMMER_REST_DEG=26deg off contact), easing there from full contact (HAMMER_ENGAGE_DEG=0) over the first REARM_MS=150ms of each RUN phase. Step 4 is RESET: over LIFT_MS=250ms (ease-out-cubic) the hammer eases further from REST(26deg) to WINDUP(34deg) — a real, visible departure; over the following STRIKE_MS=200ms (ease-in-cubic, accelerating into contact) it swings from WINDUP(34deg) down through REST and on into ENGAGE(0deg contact) while the needle+cam group's angle eases from 152deg to 0deg on the exact SAME clock, so the two complete together at hammer contact, never before it — this simultaneity is the load-bearing detail. A 200ms opacity pulse (FLASH_MS, driven by a computed 0..1 'flash' value applied straight to a small circle's opacity, max 0.55, never CSS keyframes tied to wall-clock) lights the cam's tip right after contact. Step 5 is HOLD: hammer stays engaged at contact, needle stays at zero, a beat of stillness before the wheel indexes into the next RUN phase. GEOMETRY: single 0..200 viewBox, scaled by the SVG's own preserveAspectRatio (no ResizeObserver needed for pure vector content). Column wheel hexagon at (58,148); heart cam + needle share one rotated group at (112,66) (cam drawn as a two-lobe bezier path with its point at local (0,-30)); hammer pivots at (140,22) with its UNROTATED line already pointing at the cam's tip (112,36) — hammerAngle is authored as an offset FROM that contact pose, so 0 means touching and every positive value swings the tip away along an arc, which is what lets one signed number drive lift, windup and contact without a second variable. TOKENS: column wheel and the running needle+cam — the quieter, structural, ambient 'it's alive' motion — render in var(--ns-muted); the hammer and the contact-moment flash — the fast, climactic motion — render in var(--foreground), referenced directly as CSS custom properties in the SVG markup (no getComputedStyle/MutationObserver plumbing — that machinery is for canvas/WebGL reading tokens into raw pixel values once; plain var(--token) in DOM/SVG repaints for free on a theme class switch). var(--border) is never used as a stroke; var(--ns-accent) never appears anywhere, since there is no pointer-driven highlight to reserve it for — the component takes no pointer input. prefers-reduced-motion (and paused) freeze at STATIC_MS = RESET_START_MS + LIFT_MS = 3250ms — hammer at full windup, needle/cam just starting its snap toward zero, wheel mid-step: the single most information-dense frame, never t0. An IntersectionObserver (threshold 0) and visibilitychange both stop the single rAF loop when offscreen/hidden; a 100ms poll picks up paused and an external `trigger` prop change without tearing down the effect — changing `trigger` jumps straight to RESET_START_MS instead of waiting on the idle cycle, then the ordinary loop resumes from there. role=status aria-live=polite wraps the chip; an sr-only live span announces `label` (default 'Saved') once per completed reset, not once per frame of it.
useWhen: Pick column-wheel-heart-reset when a save/confirm moment should read as a real mechanical correction — a value visibly snapping back to a known-good zero regardless of where it drifted, then staying there through a held beat. Pick confirm-hold-ink instead for a press-and-hold destructive confirmation (the mechanism here has no pointer input at all); pick notification-bell-swing instead when the feedback moment is arrival-driven (badge counts, a physical bell ring per event) rather than a single self-correcting reset.
